findings.title: Require an error-only filter instead of a substring match
findings.body: The substring check also accepts queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. For allowlisted projects, these queries consequently have count() replaced with the error-only sample_weight aggregation even though they can select transactions, where sample_weight is unsupported. This can break valid Discover queries or return incorrect counts. Eligibility needs to establish from the parsed filter that every matching event is an error, accounting for negation and OR branches.

findings.title: Apply upsampling to top-N selection, not just its time series
findings.body: Only timeseries_columns are transformed; selected_columns and orderby still contain the original count() aggregation. A request grouping by issue and ordering by descending count therefore selects top issues by ingested event count but displays their upsampled counts. With varying sampling rates, an issue containing one event of weight 10 can be excluded in favor of an issue containing two events of weight 1. Transform the aggregation used for top-N selection as well so selection and displayed counts use the same measure.

findings.title: Check the dataset actually used for split dashboard queries
findings.body: The eligibility check receives the enclosing request's dataset rather than scoped_dataset. For a metrics-enhanced dashboard request whose widget is split to ERROR_EVENTS, get_event_stats_factory explicitly executes the query against Discover, but this check still sees the metrics dataset and always rejects upsampling. Even with allowlisted projects and an explicit event.type:error filter, that error chart returns raw sampled counts. Base eligibility on the dataset and effective query actually being executed.

findings.title: Verify counting of unsampled historical errors
findings.body: Both fixture events have client_sample_rate=0.1, so the tests only verify rows with explicit sampling metadata. Allowlisting a project also affects queries over its pre-rollout errors, which lack that metadata. The new aggregation directly sums sample_weight and relies on a schema-default assumption that these tests never verify. Add an allowlisted-project test with unsampled errors, including a mixture of sampled and unsampled rows, and assert that each unsampled error still contributes one to the count.
